closures.observed_ui01_evidence: ROLE_ENTRY mapped BOTH merchant_branch and merchant_human_resource to BranchLayout, and router/routes/hr.ts imported that layout directly. Every other account had a layout of its own, so Human Resource was the one account presenting under another account's identity. The account host registry compounded it by naming the account 'HR'.
closures.root_cause: Only one layout was authored for the two branch-scoped accounts, and the account contract recorded that sharing as if it were intentional.
closures.why_this_is_the_root_cause: The navigation data was already role-specific — `navigationFor('merchant_human_resource')` returns HR's own items. What was shared was the IDENTITY: the layout name in ROLE_ENTRY, the route's layout import, and the display name. Correcting the navigation would have changed nothing, because the navigation was never wrong.
closures.correct_fix: A compositional correction, not a copy. HumanResourceLayout delegates to the same shared RoleShell every sibling layout uses, so there is no second shell to keep in step. ROLE_ENTRY now names that layout and the label 'Human Resource'; hr.ts imports it; config/account-hosts.json (the UI-02 authority) carries the corrected display name and the generated registry was regenerated from it.

closures.observed_ui01_evidence: With colorScheme dark and no stored preference, the root element carried class 'dark' at first paint and rendered dark. The pre-hydration script read window.matchMedia('(prefers-color-scheme: dark)') and applied dark when no stored value existed.
closures.root_cause: The pre-hydration script applied dark when `stored` was absent and `prefersDark` was true. The condition should have depended on the stored value alone. The same rule was duplicated in themeStore.resolveInitial().
closures.why_this_is_the_root_cause: Two independent places consulted the operating system, and BOTH had to change: correcting only the inline script would have left hydration flipping the theme back, which is the flash the ADR also forbids.
closures.correct_fix: The bootstrap now reads, in order: the server-rendered data-sv-theme attribute, then the explicit per-browser value, then light. It is byte-identical in both shells. The store mirrors that precedence exactly so hydration cannot change what was painted. `matchMedia` and `prefers-color-scheme` appear in neither shell, neither store, nor the generated token CSS. Authenticated persistence was added as the smallest self-owned contract: a nullable, CHECK-constrained users.theme_preference, PATCH /api/v1/auth/preferences (own scope, NO permission key), and the value exposed through /me.

closures.before: Clean browser + dark OS => dark at first paint.
closures.after: Clean browser + dark OS => LIGHT, verified in a real Chromium context with colorScheme: 'dark', and the store proven never to CALL matchMedia at all.
closures.permission_impact: None. Changing your own display preference is authorized by ownership; the request carries no user identifier.

closures.observed_ui01_evidence: android-chrome-192x192.png and android-chrome-512x512.png are approved and present, but no source file or HTML head referenced them. No web app manifest existed.
closures.root_cause: The SPA head declared favicon.ico, the 16px and 32px PNGs and the apple-touch-icon, but no web app manifest existed to reference the Android icons.
closures.why_this_is_the_root_cause: The Android icons are only reachable through a manifest; adding more <link rel=icon> tags would not have made them installable.
closures.correct_fix: public/assets/brand/site.webmanifest, linked from BOTH shells. It lives under /assets/ because that prefix is backend-owned in both topologies — a manifest at the document root would fall through to the SPA fallback and be served as HTML. nginx 1.27 has no .webmanifest MIME entry, so `application/manifest+json` is declared explicitly; without it the file is served as octet-stream and, because the /assets/ location sets nosniff, the browser refuses to parse it. `display: browser` is the honest value: no service worker is registered and no offline capability is claimed.

closures.observed_ui01_evidence: Thirteen uncaught TypeErrors across twelve detail and summary routes, each an unguarded dereference of a nested money object or a collection under the repository's own canonical e2e fixtures.
closures.root_cause:
Two distinct causes, settled against the backend contract rather than guessed:
(a) GENUINELY OPTIONAL FIELDS treated as required — CashUpResource exposes `lines` through whenLoaded, so it is absent whenever the relation was not eager-loaded; InvoiceResource and InvoiceItemResource declare `preferred_personnel_fee` explicitly nullable.
(b) A PAYLOAD SHAPE the contract never produces — the shared audit fixture falls back to an empty paginated envelope for an unmatched GET, so a detail route received a collection where an object belongs.
closures.why_this_is_the_root_cause: For (a) the component was simply wrong: the server can and does omit those fields. For (b) the screen must still degrade rather than throw — which is exactly the acceptance test UI-01 wrote for this defect: 'Each affected route renders with an incomplete payload and produces no uncaught exception, showing a defined empty state instead.'
closures.correct_fix: Twenty-eight targeted guards across ten components, each at ONE proven expression — no blanket optional-chaining sweep. Money now renders through SvMoney, which shows 'Not available' for an absent amount and NEVER coerces it to zero: a false financial figure would be worse than the TypeError it replaced. RecordPayment received the sharpest correction — `invoice.balance.amount ?? 0` would have read as 'fully paid' and silently forbidden a legitimate payment, so an unknown balance now blocks submission with a stated reason.

Running the closure spec then reached FURTHER unguarded money renders on InvoiceDetail and RecordPayment — sites the audit never reached because the first exception stopped the render. Guarding only what the audit happened to hit first would have left both routes still able to throw, so every remaining nested money render on those screens was migrated too.

closures.found_by: Phase UI-04 raw-value source guard, while migrating components onto semantic tokens.
closures.observed_problem: Sixteen `var(--custom, #hex)` fallbacks across fourteen pages referenced custom properties that were NEVER DEFINED anywhere — `--color-danger` and `--color-focus` do not exist in any stylesheet. The literal fallback was therefore LIVE, not dead: those pages rendered a non-brand `#dc2626` and a generic blue `#2563eb` focus ring, neither of which is a Servana token, and neither of which had a dark-theme value.
closures.root_cause: The fallbacks were written defensively against variables that were assumed to exist. Nothing verified the assumption, and a fallback that always fires is indistinguishable from a hard-coded colour.
closures.why_this_is_the_root_cause: The undefined variables are the whole mechanism: had `--color-danger` and `--color-focus` existed, the fallbacks would have been inert. The generic blue focus ring in particular bypassed the entire theme layer, so it did not change in dark mode and had never been contrast-checked.
closures.correct_fix: All sixteen usages migrated to semantic Tailwind aliases and CSS custom properties backed by the token authority. `DesignTokenSourceGuardTest` now fails the build on any raw hex in production UI source, with negative controls proving the matcher fires.
files_changed: 14 page components across branch, finance, payments, merchant and platform

closures.found_by: Phase UI-04, while bringing SvToast up to the shared component contract.
closures.observed_problem: Four contract defects in the Phase 4 toast: (1) status was carried by a coloured dot ALONE, with no text or icon; (2) the container was aria-live AND each toast was role=status, nesting a live region inside a live region so every message was announced twice; (3) it was positioned `bottom-4`, inside the band the fixed footer occupies, so its dismiss control could be covered — a case ADR-024 names explicitly; (4) removal was scheduled only on mount, so any toast added afterwards never expired.
closures.root_cause: The component predates both the fixed-footer contract and the icon system, and its live-region nesting was never exercised by a test.
closures.correct_fix: Heroicon plus a visually hidden severity word; a single live region; a bottom offset computed from the SAME footer-height token the page reserves; a watcher that schedules newly added toasts and clears timers for removed ones; the 20px hand-rolled SVG close control replaced with SvIconButton at the 44px minimum.

closures.observed_ui01_evidence: Not a UI-01 defect. Found by the final full Playwright gate (~30 failures at the tablet boundary).
closures.root_cause: The SvProfileControl identity block is hidden md:block, so 768px is the first width at which it renders. The inline-flex trigger sizes to its content and truncate does not engage without a bounded width, so a long display name made the trigger 562px wide and the header overflowed (scrollWidth 775 > clientWidth 768).
closures.why_this_is_the_root_cause: The widest-element chain named the trigger button directly, and the overflow appeared at exactly the breakpoint that first reveals the block.
closures.correct_fix: Added a profile-identity-max-width layout token wired through Tailwind maxWidth, so the cap comes from the token authority rather than a literal, plus min-w-0 on the shrinkable ancestors so the text ellipsises instead of dictating header width.
tests: full Playwright responsive matrix at 360/768/1280
closures.before: Every shell-bearing screen scrolled horizontally at 768px.
closures.after: No horizontal overflow at any audited width.
